card.name: Linking words before QT arrhythmia terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (an opening parenthesis, "such as", "due to", "and", "e.g.,") right before a named arrhythmia such as torsades de pointes, ventricular tachycardia or sudden death, in QT-prolongation warnings.

modes.label: Bracket or list opener
modes.description: An opening parenthesis or "such as" that introduces torsades de pointes or an example drug.
modes.example: usually in association with QT prolongation<< (>>torsades de pointes), but sometimes

modes.label: Cause or link words
modes.description: Words like "to" or "and" that link a cause to ventricular arrhythmia or sudden death.
modes.example: due to the risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias<< and>> sudden death potentially associated with elevated plasma levels

card.writes: It seems to push toward adverbs and Chinese word starts, and away from paralysis and nerve terms, so it adds no clear heart-specific word.
card.plain: It lights up on the small connecting words just before a heart rhythm danger like torsades is named.
